A large indoor display wall showing a curated collage of historical and project photographs mounted on a teal-green backdrop printed with faint white circuit-like lines, concentric arcs and repeating binary digits ("0" and "1"). The wall is a timeline/commemorative panel — photos are arranged in a loose grid with small rectangular blue caption strips below many images. The teal background, white graphic lines and binary text give a technological / engineering theme; the top edge of the photo shows a red ceiling trim and part of an HVAC vent, confirming the installation is inside a building.

Overall layout and color:
- The backdrop is a muted teal with white linework and binary-code motifs. Photos are mostly rectangular, full-color prints with modest white margins; many have small blue caption labels with white text beneath them.
- Photographs vary in size. A single tall, older-looking building photo occupies the center of the arrangement and acts as a visual anchor; smaller documentary images surround it in roughly three vertical bands.
- The panel contains roughly a dozen distinct photographs depicting people at work, group shots, ceremonies, laboratory scenes, outdoor fieldwork, and a historical campus shot.

Key photos and visible subjects (clockwise from upper-left area toward lower-right):
- Upper-left area: a horizontal photo of several people working outdoors — individuals wearing sun hats and using shovels and wheelbarrows on a dirt site. A small blue caption under this image appears to read "Project Mingde" (or a similar project name).
- Top-center: a stage/ceremony photo showing a line of people in formal attire on a stage with flowers at the front. A blue caption strip beneath this reads something like "25th Anniversary of Department of Industrial and Manufacturing Systems Engineering" (the long institutional phrasing is visible).
- Upper-right: a group photo of many people outdoors in a wooded or rural setting. The small caption to its right/underneath includes the words "HKU Engineering students in Thailand to build a small-scale hydro-power system for a rural village" (the caption’s subject about students and a Thai project is readable).
- Middle-right column: a vertical photo of two people working at lab instrumentation — one seated, one watching — with a caption strip that clearly reads "Laboratory of Mechanical Engineering."
- Just above that is a darker, candid night/time photo of a lively small group crouched on steps or around an outdoor area; the caption nearby suggests a student design or "junkyard challenge" for freshmen in a mechanical engineering context.
- Center: a prominent, slightly sepia-toned photograph of a multistory brick building (an academic or administrative building). A blue caption beneath it reads something like "Chow Yiu Ching Building 1985" (a building name and date are visible).
- Mid-left: a photo showing a busy outdoor scene with vehicles and people clustered — possibly a demonstration, competition or open-day event; it sits left of the central building image.
- Lower-left: a vertical photo inside a lab or workshop showing students conducting bench experiments — hands-on apparatus, tubing and bottles visible. A blue caption beneath this references an "Environmental Biotechnology Laboratory" and a year in the late 1990s (the caption appears to read "Students conducted experiments in the Environmental Biotechnology Laboratory, 1999").
- Lower-center: a small horizontal photo of a person (face partially obscured in the image) wearing a headset or microphone, one hand raised — looks like a presentation or demonstration moment.
- Lower-right: a horizontal group photo of a large cohort of people posed outside in front of an older campus building; the blue caption underneath reads "Industrial training to Tsinghua University, 1994."

Other visible elements:
- Many individuals in the photos wear casual clothing, laboratory coats or formal attire depending on the event; several images show active hands-on work (shoveling, laboratory experiments, machinery operation).
- Small caption strips in consistent blue/white styling tie the images together and indicate these photos are part of a curated institutional timeline or departmental history.
- The overall composition is documentary and archival in nature: a combination of student activities, research/lab scenes, community projects, formal ceremonies and historical campus architecture, presented to tell a department or faculty story.

Location/context inference:
- The graphic styling, captions referencing departments and engineering activities, and the mix of lab, classroom, fieldwork and campus images indicate this is an informational/history display in an academic engineering department or faculty corridor. The presence of specific captions (e.g., "Laboratory of Mechanical Engineering," building name and anniversary text) supports that this is a university engineering department exhibit summarizing projects, student activities, training exchanges and historical milestones.

A photographic poster-style collage documenting an institutional opening ceremony and associated talks, shown at an angle on a glossy mounted board. The board is divided into multiple rectangular panels with caption strips beneath each image; the overall background of the board is white with purple accent lines and a purple lower border.

Top row, center-right: the largest photo is a formal group portrait taken in front of a deep blue, starry patterned banner that reads in large white type, “TAM WING FAN INNOVATION WING TWO OPENING CEREMONY” with a smaller line underneath showing the date “28th December 2021.” About 30–40 adults (business/academic attire) are arranged in two rows — seated front row and standing back row — most giving a thumbs-up gesture. Nearly all visible people are wearing surgical or disposable face masks. Attire is mostly dark suits and formal jackets; the scene is indoors under bright even lighting.

Top row, left: a smaller rectangular photo shows another group shot of seated people before a vertical banner that reads “Tam Wing Fan Inno Wing Two” and “FACULTY OF ENGINEERING.” That image is narrower and framed with a thin orange accent at the top of the photo.

Middle row, left and center: two smaller panels show speakers giving presentations. One panel captures a presenter gesturing at a projected slide with a semi-transparent human figure and technical visuals; the caption beneath reads “Tech Talk – Professor Norman C. Tien.” The adjacent panel shows another presenter beside a slide with digital/blue circuitry imagery and overlaid text; a portion of the slide’s visible text reads “Digitizing detection by breaking up body fluids, such as blood, into millions and trillions of droplets.” Its caption reads “Tech Talk – Professor Anderson H.C. Shum.” In both panels the speakers are wearing business attire and face masks; the slide backgrounds are blue and high-contrast.

Middle row, right: a wide rectangular photo depicts an audience seated in a modern lecture / event space watching a speaker standing to the right of the frame. The audience seating, flooring and visible architecture suggest an indoor institutional venue; a blue wall feature with partial text “On the edge of …” and an “HKU” logo area are visible in the background.

Across the lower portion of the board are caption strips: directly beneath the top group photo is a printed caption line reading “Opening Ceremony for Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing Two, 2021.” Individual caption boxes appear beneath each tech-talk image with the speaker names as noted above; another caption beneath the audience photo reads “Tech Talk – Professor Yuguo Li.”

Foreground and mounting context: the photographed poster sits near floor level and the camera captures part of the surrounding setup — a black metal stand or monitor mount on the left edge, coiled cables, and a small yellow safety sticker or tape on a black base (bottom-left of the photo). There is slight reflection and gloss on the poster surface and the whole image is shot at an oblique angle, so the panels appear trapezoidal and the lower edge of the board and the floor are visible.

Color and composition notes: dominant colors are white (board), purple (accents and lower border), and deep blue (large ceremony backdrop and presentation slides). The collage composition is formal and documentary — a sequence of event images with descriptive captions conveying an opening ceremony plus a series of associated technical talks at an engineering faculty venue. Several faces in the printed photos appear intentionally blurred in the captured image, and most visible attendees wear face masks, indicating COVID-era precautions.

A large indoor exhibition or history wall, likely inside a university building, photographed straight-on from a short distance. The wall is a curated collage of archival photographs, sketches and newspaper clippings mounted against a teal-to-aqua graphic background that includes repeating binary digits ("0" and "1") and thin white circuit-like lines and concentric rings as a visual motif.

Overall layout and composition
- The display is arranged in a loose grid of framed images and caption strips, with larger rectangular pictures occupying the central vertical band and smaller documentary photos grouped to the right and bottom. White borders surround each photo panel, and many images have small rectangular blue caption labels directly beneath them.
- The top of the photograph shows part of the ceiling: linear ventilation grilles and a white directional spotlight that casts a bright glare on one of the mounted prints (a white reflection is visible on the upper center image).
- The lower edge of the frame shows a short blue baseboard belonging to the wall.

Key images and visible content (left-to-right, top-to-bottom)
- Top-left: A yellowed newspaper front or clipping with a visible headline “Student Extra.” Smaller text beneath suggests a story about a new department for HKU (the words “New department for HKU” are legible). A blue caption strip below this clipping appears to reference the establishment year.
- Top-center: An architectural rendering or watercolor of a modern multi-storey building in warm orange and terracotta tones; the perspective shows the building on a slight slope with small painted figures and landscaping around it.
- Center-left (large): A photographic image of a large concrete-and-glass academic building (dark grey/purple tonal cast) set behind wide staircases and planted greenery. A blue caption beneath this photo reads something like “Haking Wong Building, 1983.”
- Center-right: A color photo of a smaller multi-storey building with exterior red zig-zag staircases against a pale yellow façade; a blue caption strip below this notes a renaming or date (partially readable).
- Upper-right cluster: Several small photos showing groups of people — candid color images of students or staff engaged in workshop/lab activities and a black-and-white photo showing older laboratory work or machinery. These convey historical teaching and hands-on activities.
- Bottom row (left-to-right): A small photo of a person working at a CRT computer terminal (screen and keyboard visible, face blurred in the photo as captured in this display); next to it, a photo of an individual soldering or assembling electronics components at a workbench; at the far right a group of small images showing meetings, classes and a handful of smiling people gathered outdoors.

Colors and visual details
- Dominant background colors: teal, aqua, and blue with white graphic accents.
- Photographic palette varies: sepia/yellow newspaper clipping, warm orange sketch, cool-toned architectural photos (purples and greys), and natural color candid photos (skin tones, clothing).
- Graphic binary digits ("010101...") appear faintly across the teal background, reinforcing a computing or engineering theme.

Text and captions
- Legible text includes the newspaper masthead “Student Extra” and a visible phrase “New department for HKU.” Several blue caption strips are present; a few readable fragments include building names and dates (for example “Haking Wong Building, 1983”).
- Most caption text is small and not fully readable at this photograph resolution, but the consistent blue caption bars indicate descriptive labels for each image.

People and activity
- Multiple images show groups of people — students and staff appearing in lab, workshop and classroom settings. No individual identities are discernible; the photos are documentary in nature, showing collaborative and instructional activities (people seated at terminals, gathered around equipment, or posing in small groups).

Location/context inference
- The combination of “HKU” in visible text, building-photo captions, and the computing-themed graphic background suggests this is a historical/commemorative display for a university department (likely computer science or engineering) showcasing campus buildings, early labs and student life over several decades. The presence of old CRT terminals and black-and-white lab photos underscores a multi-era timeline.

Overall impression
- A professionally designed institutional timeline wall that blends archival press clippings, architectural imagery and documentary photos to tell the historical story of a university department. The teal binary background and captioned image blocks give a modern, tech-oriented visual framing while the individual photographs emphasize people, buildings and hands-on technical work across time.

A large indoor exhibition wall or museum-style mural displaying a curated collage of historical photographs and captions about an engineering school or technical workshops.

Overall scene and location context
- The image shows a section of a public interior space — a long, wall-mounted graphic panel under a ceiling air-vent and exposed sprinkler/pipe fixture. The floor visible at the bottom is a pale turquoise/teal color, matching the mural’s design palette.
- The wall graphic spans two adjacent vertical panels: the left panel has a teal-to-cyan background with faint technical/architectural linework and numerical sequences printed across it; the right panel is a lighter, desaturated grey with the same design motif. Thin white dividing lines separate and frame the individual photograph groupings.

Key objects, layout and composition
- Dominating the left half of the display is a very large sepia-toned photograph of a multi-storey institutional building (an older school or college building) mounted near the top-left quadrant. The image is rectangular and occupies a substantial portion of the left panel, acting as an anchor for the montage.
- Beneath and around that large building photo are a series of smaller historical photographs in black-and-white and sepia: workshop scenes, groups of people, outdoor shots, and classroom/lab interiors. Most small images are framed with narrow white borders and have small blue caption bars beneath them.
- The right vertical column contains a tall stacked arrangement of another set of black-and-white photos: interior workshop/classroom views, group portraits, machinery in use, and exterior shots of buildings. Nearly every photograph has a small, dark-blue caption label beneath or adjacent to it.
- The layout is grid-like but slightly staggered: images are grouped in clusters rather than a strict uniform grid, creating a museum-didactic collage that leads the eye from the large building image across the smaller documentary photos.

Colors, textures and graphic elements
- Dominant colors are teal/cyan, pale grey, white and the warm brown/orange sepia of historic photos. The teal background includes faint white technical drawing lines, node points and numerical strings (like rows of digits), giving a modern-engineering visual context behind the historic pictures.
- Photographs themselves are monochrome (black-and-white) and sepia, giving the display an archival, early-20th-century feel.
- Blue caption bars (deep navy/royal blue) appear beneath many photos; the tiny white caption text is not legible in this overall view but clearly present as explanatory labels.

People, activity and subjects shown
- The historic photos depict many people in early 20th-century clothing and workwear: small student groups, classroom scenes, shop and machinery work with visible tools or equipment, and formal group portraits of men in suits (likely faculty or graduating classes). None of the individuals are identified in the wide view; they appear as archival documentary subjects rather than contemporaneous visitors.
- Several images show hands-on technical activity — people operating or gathered around machinery and workshop benches — indicating the exhibition documents practical engineering or vocational education history.
- A surveying/outdoor scene is visible in the lower-left cluster (figures in white clothing positioned on a grass or paved area with a surveying pole or instrument).

Visible text and signage
- Small blue caption bars under the photos contain short labels and dates, though the caption text is too small in this overall photograph to be read clearly. The large sepia building photograph has printed signage across the facade in the photo itself (an institutional name on the building), but the letters are not fully legible at this resolution.
- The mural’s background also includes faint numerical sequences and schematic lines as a decorative/interpretive element, rather than large readable copy.

Ceiling and environmental details
- At the very top of the photograph, an air-conditioning vent grille runs horizontally across the ceiling above the mural; an exposed sprinkler head and a short pipe drop are visible, indicating a modern interior retrofit.
- Lighting in the space is even and diffuse, with no strong shadows — typical of a gallery or display corridor.

Overall impression
- The composition reads as an interpretive, educational panel commemorating the history of an engineering or technical school: a prominent archival image of the school building anchors the display, supported by documentary snapshots of classrooms, workshops, fieldwork and formal group portraits. The modern turquoise/teal graphic background, technical linework and blue caption bars combine archival content with contemporary exhibit design.

A large printed display panel showing a collage of formal event photographs and captions, arranged on a pale grey background with subtle white contour lines and a colored header band (turquoise and dark blue) along the top edge.

Overall layout and appearance
- The panel contains five distinct photographs arranged in a loose grid: two small photos at the top, one large wide photo in the middle, and two smaller photos along the bottom row (left and right). Thin blue caption bars with white text appear beneath several photos identifying the events and year.
- The overall design uses a corporate/university visual style: clean light-grey background, blue accent bars for captions, and printed photo borders. A banner or backdrop with institutional logos appears in several of the pictures.
- Colors across the panel are mainly neutral and formal — suits in black/navy/grey, white shirts, and darker tie colors — punctuated by the turquoise/dark-blue header, some red carpeting in one photo, and natural brick and greenery in an outdoor shot.

Top-left photo (cheque presentation)
- A medium-sized indoor portrait showing five standing adults and one seated person (faces blurred in this reproduction). They are dressed in formal business attire (suits, ties, and a knee-length skirt for one person).
- The central object is an oversized ceremonial cheque being held horizontally by two people. The cheque has printed text including “The University of Hong Kong” and the amount spelled out as “One Hundred Million Only.” A small date line and signature block are visible at the top-right area of the cheque.
- The setting looks like an office or reception room with warm wood doors and framed artwork on the wall behind the group. A small caption bar beneath this photo reads “Cheque Presentation Ceremony, 2017.”

Top-right photo (outdoor group)
- A smaller outdoor group photo showing roughly 30–40 people standing on a brick-paved courtyard between modern brick-and-concrete buildings. Many people are holding round hand-held signs with bold lettering; a small wheeled robot or piece of equipment sits on the ground in front of the group.
- The overall mood is informal and celebratory; the caption beneath this image reads “First Engineering Inno Show, 2019.”

Center (large group/dedication ceremony)
- The largest photograph dominates the middle of the panel and is an indoor formal group portrait of approximately 50–60 people arranged in multiple rows. The front row consists of seated dignitaries (including an elderly gentleman in a wheelchair and other seated older adults), while several rows of standing participants fill the background.
- Most attendees wear business attire and name badges; a mix of men and women is present. A stage backdrop behind them displays a banner with logos and bilingual text (English and Chinese) and includes the phrases “Faculty of Engineering” and references to a “Dedication Ceremony.” The caption under this photo reads “Dedication Ceremony for Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing, 2018.”
- The photograph has warm indoor lighting and a formal composition typical of institutional dedication or opening ceremonies.

Bottom-left photo (hard-hat group)
- A small indoor photo showing about 12–15 people posed in a bright, modern interior space with white walls and angled blue architectural features. Several seated and standing participants hold white safety helmets (construction hard hats) on their laps or in their hands, suggesting a site visit or handover related to facilities/innovation spaces.
- Participants are dressed in business-casual to formal attire; the space looks newly finished or recently renovated.

Bottom-right photo (red-carpet dedication)
- Another small indoor formal photo taken in front of a printed backdrop with logos and bilingual text. A group of around 10–15 people stands behind and beside an elderly seated man in a wheelchair who appears again (the same individual appears multiple times across the panel). Several people wear boutonnieres or lapel flowers, and the floor is covered with a short red carpet in front of the backdrop.
- This image also conveys a formal dedication or celebratory opening; the caption beneath it again references the “Faculty of Engineering” and a dedication ceremony.

Additional visible text and logos
- Recurrent text elements include “Faculty of Engineering” and institutional logos on event backdrops, as well as photo captions: “Cheque Presentation Ceremony, 2017,” “First Engineering Inno Show, 2019,” and “Dedication Ceremony for Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing, 2018.”
- The oversized cheque in the top-left photo clearly shows “The University of Hong Kong” and the spelled-out amount “One Hundred Million Only.”

People, clothing and props
- Across the collage most people are adults in formal or business-casual clothing: dark suits, ties, blazers, dresses, and name badges. Several individuals appear in multiple photos (notably an elderly seated gentleman in a wheelchair), indicating recurring participation in the documented events.
- Props and visual cues include an oversized ceremonial cheque, hard hats, hand-held event signs, a small robot/equipment in the outdoor shot, stage/backdrop banners with logos, and floral boutonnieres on some attendees.

Location and context
- The collection of images documents official university or faculty events — a major donation/cheque presentation, an innovation/showcase event outdoors, and multiple dedication/opening ceremonies for an “Innovation Wing.” Settings alternate between formal indoor event halls with branded backdrops, a bright contemporary interior, and an outdoor brick courtyard on campus.
- The overall impression is a timeline-style display highlighting milestones and ceremonies related to a university engineering faculty’s facilities and innovation activities.

A large indoor documentary display panel mounted on a wall in a modern building corridor. The display is a tall vertical poster made up of a white background with a faint hexagonal pattern and a sweeping purple-to-blue wave graphic across the top. The poster is divided into a grid of labeled event photographs (each photo has a thin white border and a short caption beneath it) that document a series of academic/ceremonial events.

Top area
- A horizontal band of purple/blue gradient waves runs along the very top of the panel, providing a visual header.
- In the top-left quadrant there is a photo of people gathered around a long table with models and equipment; the caption underneath reads something like "Engineering Inno Show, 2020."
- To the right of that is a smaller photo showing a few formally dressed people standing together, with the caption “Plaque Unveiling at Opening Ceremony for Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing, 2020.”

Center area
- A prominent central group photograph shows a large seated-and-standing assembly of people (several rows) posed for an official group shot; most people in the photos are wearing face masks and formal or business-casual attire. A banner or title line above this central image references the "Opening Ceremony for Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing" and includes a university crest/logo at the top.
- Surrounding the central group shot are other smaller images from the same series of events: ribbon/bell/award moments, smaller groups of officials posing in front of a backdrop, and people receiving certificates or plaques.

Lower area
- Along the lower portion of the panel are two donation/award photographs with captions referencing "Innovation Academy" and donation acknowledgements dated 2021. One caption reads "Donation from Mrs May Tam in support of Innovation Academy, 2021" and another states "Donation from Philomathia Foundation in support of Innovation Academy, 2021."
- A pair of photos on the bottom-left show two people holding a certificate or framed document; in one of those lower photos the faces of the persons appear intentionally blurred or obscured in the printed image.
- Another lower photo shows a group of people (again masked) holding an oversized ceremonial cheque or plaque and posing for the camera.

People and attire
- Across the photographs, subjects are mostly adult professionals wearing suits, blazers, and business clothing. Nearly all photographed people are wearing face masks (consistent with pandemic-era events).
- Poses vary between formal standing poses, seated group rows for official shots, and candid moments of unveiling, presenting documents, or small-group discussions around tables.

Text and logos visible
- Captions visible on the panel include references to "Tam Wing Fan Innovation Wing," "Opening Ceremony," "Innovation Academy," "Faculty of Engineering, HKU," and donation acknowledgements with years (2020, 2021).
- A university crest/logo appears on one of the event captions/headers (consistent with an academic institution’s display).

Surrounding environment and architectural context
- The display sits under a red ceiling section with a visible linear air vent near the top left of the photograph.
- To the right of the panel is an open corridor with glass partitions and a teal/aqua colored interior visible beyond the glass; part of a doorway or signage area is visible down the corridor.
- The floor in front of the display is carpeted with a tactile guiding strip (raised lines) running parallel to the display, indicating a public interior space designed for accessibility (likely a university or institutional building interior).
- Lighting is bright and even; the display appears to be behind a clear protective face or framed by trim along its edges.

Overall composition and impression
- The photograph emphasizes institutional memory and publicity: a curated collage of event photos, group portraits, and captions celebrating the opening of an "Innovation Wing" and later donations to an "Innovation Academy."
- Color accents are dominated by the white panel background and cool blue/purple header, contrasted with the warm red of the ceiling and muted corridor tones. The arrangement is orderly and documentary in style, intended to inform viewers walking past about recent milestones and ceremonies.

A tilted oblique photograph of a projected presentation slide on an interior wall or screen. The slide is a collage of event photos and captions from 2021, dominated by pale blue, white and soft purple graphic elements with a thin purple curved banner along the top edge. A black speaker cabinet is visible at the left edge of the frame and a red ceiling panel runs along the upper-left corner, giving context that the picture was taken inside a room or hall. A large dark shadow — likely a person standing between the projector and the screen — falls across the lower-middle area of the projection, partially obscuring one of the photos.

Top-right panel: a rectangular image showing two seated, formally dressed adults engaged in a stage-style conversation. Both figures are seated on simple black chairs with a small round side table between them holding a small potted plant. One person appears to be holding a microphone; both wear dark business attire. Above that image is a heading in navy text that reads, in part, “Making Impact in a Technology-Driven World My Leadership Journey in Academia” and a date line “February 3, 2021.” The University of Hong Kong crest and Chinese/English name appear near the top of the slide.

Top-left and lower sections: multiple group photographs of large cohorts (several dozen people total) posed indoors. Most people in these group photos are wearing face masks and formal or business-casual clothing; many are seated in front rows with others standing behind them, and several participants make thumbs-up gestures. Captions beneath the images read “Inaugural InnoSharing, 2021” (center) and “InnoHub Kick-off Event, 2021” (below the largest group photo). The group images are framed with thin white borders and set against the slide’s pale background.

Other visible details: the slide layout includes hexagonal faint background motifs and thin accent lines in purple. Colors in the projected images are slightly washed and skewed by the angle of the photograph; the blue tones of the slide’s background and the white projection surface dominate. A small portion of another framed image or poster appears at the extreme lower-left corner, cropped out. Several faces in the projection are blurred or indistinct because of distance, projection softness and the overlying shadow. Overall the scene conveys a formal university event presentation summarizing InnoSharing / InnoHub activities in 2021, with a mix of staged panel discussion imagery and masked group photos.
